newsitem.title: USA: American Dental can't explain stock drop. [CORRECTED 14:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: American Dental can't explain stock drop. [CORRECTED 14:00 GMT]

text.p: American Dental Technologies Inc said Friday it knew of no reason for the recent decline in its stock price.

"In light of our recent reports of record earnings and FDA (U.S. Food and Drug Administration) clearance of our Nd:YAG lasers for laser curettage, the company knows of no reason for the recent decline in stock price," President Ben Gallant said in a statement.
The stock closed Thursday at $5 a share, near its 52-week low.

American Dental, which develops and makes advanced technologies for dentistry and markets them worldwide, said the FDA recently cleared an Erbium YAG laser for use on teeth. American Dental owns the patents on the laser, but the approval was received by another company, Premium Laser Systems Inc. (Corrects to clarify that Premium Laser Systems, not American Dental, was the recipient of the FDA approval.)

"While we hold the basic patents in this area of technology, experience has shown in Europe and in the Pacific Rim over the last several years that the Erbium YAG laser has had serious limitations, insignificant penetration of the dental market, and negligible effect in our sales of KCP air abrasive systems for hard tissue applications," Gallant said. "Due to the superior performance and cost advantage of our KCP system, we have chosen not to exploit our patents at this time."
However, the company is "well positioned" to exploit this technology when it becomes commercially viable, he added.
